Thursday, November 19

Game recap

BOS4DET1Final: BOS 4, DET 1

Detroit threw itself a 100th birthday party and Boston ate the cake. The Red Wings' Centennial Celebration Game started on script, Lucas Raymond scoring his ninth late in the first, and then the Bruins scored the next four like guests who found the open bar. JJ Peterka tied it early in the second, Pavel Zacha put Boston ahead on the power play, David Pastrnak buried his 10th in the third and Casey Mittelstadt hit the empty net, with Zacha, Pastrnak and Mittelstadt each adding an assist. Mason Lohrei and Morgan Geekie had two helpers apiece. Jeremy Swayman, on the second night of a back-to-back, stopped 20 of 21, which is less a workload than a light jog. Daniil Tarasov made 27 saves on 30 shots and deserved a better party. Boston's three-game skid is over, 4-1. Detroit has a century of history and one goal to show for the night: the franchise turned 100, and the offense skated like it.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

MTL3NJD2Final: MTL 3, NJD 2

Lane Hutson didn't score and still ran the building. The Canadiens defenseman set up all three Montreal goals in a 3-2 win in Newark, handing Connor Hellebuyck his first loss as a Devil. The first period was a track meet: Luke Evangelista opened the scoring, Alex Newhook answered 40 seconds later, Timo Meier put New Jersey back in front, and Nick Suzuki tied it on the power play with 42 seconds left before the break. Then everybody remembered defense existed, until Jake Evans scored the winner 6:17 into the third. Jacob Fowler stopped 28 of 30 for Montreal; Hellebuyck stopped 25 of 28. Jack Hughes fired four shots, won a quarter of his faceoffs and went home with nothing. The Devils finally have their goalie in the crease, and the skaters picked that night to take one off. That's New Jersey for you: fix the roof, leave the windows open.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

COL1UTA4Final: COL 1, UTA 4

Utah's six-game winless streak died the way hockey intended: a fourth-liner's goal and a fistfight four seconds later. Liam O'Brien scored his first of the season 5:22 into the second, Jack McBain and Gabriel Landeskog dropped the gloves before the goal was announced, and the Mammoth rolled to a 4-1 win. Vincent Trocheck added a power-play goal late in the period, O'Brien celebrated by fighting Alex Gagne 38 seconds after that, and Trocheck set up Dmitri Simashev shorthanded a minute into the third. Sebastian Cossa stopped 30 of 31, losing the shutout to Jaden Schwartz with five minutes left, and Kevin Stenlund hit the empty net. Mackenzie Blackwood made 25 saves on 28 shots. Colorado gave up goals at even strength, on the penalty kill and on its own power play. That's not a loss, that's a sampler platter.

Wednesday, November 18

Game recap

LAK3BOS0Final: LAK 3, BOS 0

Darcy Kuemper walked into TD Garden, stopped all 29 shots for his 40th career shutout, then picked up an assist on the empty-netter, which means the Kings' goalie outscored the entire Bruins roster. Mats Zuccarello opened the scoring late in the first off a feed from Erik Gustafsson, who was back after three games out. Andre Lee made it 2-0 late in the second, and Gustafsson finished it into the empty net with Kuemper getting the helper. Los Angeles ends a four-game losing streak. Michael DiPietro did his part, 19 saves on 21, and got the run support of a man jogging alone. Marco Sturm reunited David Pastrnak, Elias Lindholm and Morgan Geekie, and the reunion tour sold zero tickets. That's three straight losses for Boston, which now heads to Detroit's centennial party as the guest who forgot to bring a gift, or a goal.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

EDM5FLA2Final: EDM 5, FLA 2

Connor McDavid ran his point streak to 23 games and passed Wayne Gretzky for the Oilers' record in power-play points along the way, the kind of sentence you only get to write about one guy. Edmonton was up 4-0 before Florida found the building: Kasperi Kapanen opened it, McDavid scored on the power play, and Vasily Podkolzin scored twice in the second, his 11th and 12th, one of them on the power play too. Podkolzin, Kapanen and Leon Draisaitl all finished with three points. Matthew Tkachuk scored twice in the last seven minutes to push his own point streak to nine games, and Draisaitl's 21st into the empty net ended the suspense. Devon Levi stopped 20 of 22. Jacob Markstrom stopped 13 of 17, a .765 that plays as a batting average and nowhere else. The Panthers took almost 54 minutes to show up to their own home game, which in South Florida still counts as early.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

CBJ1NYI5Final: CBJ 1, NYI 5

Matthew Schaefer scored his first career hat trick, the first by an Islanders defenseman since Denis Potvin in 1982, and when the comparison is Potvin you can stop the scouting report there. He scored unassisted early in the second for a 2-0 lead, restored the two-goal cushion in the third after Zach Werenski had cut it to 2-1, and finished into the empty net, his ninth of the season on nine shots on goal for the night. Anthony Duclair opened the scoring on a power play with 58 seconds left in the first, Tony DeAngelo added one, Mathew Barzal had two assists, and Ilya Sorokin stopped 28 of 29. Cam Talbot faced 40 shots, stopped 36 and should file for hazard pay. That's five straight regulation losses for Columbus. The Blue Jackets have finally found consistency. It's just the wrong kind.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

BUF3PHI4Final: BUF 3, PHI 4

The Sabres led 47 seconds in, led again midway through the second, and lost anyway, because Buffalo handles a lead like a hot pan. Mattias Samuelsson opened the scoring, Jamie Drysdale tied it, Tage Thompson's 13th put Buffalo back in front, and Owen Tippett tied it again. Travis Sanheim gave Philadelphia its first lead 29 seconds into the third, Jiri Kulich answered with his first goal in 11 games, and Christian Dvorak won it 52 seconds after that. Matvei Michkov's two assists stretched his point streak to five games. Nobody is framing the goalie lines: Joseph Woll stopped 16 of 19 and won, Alex Lyon stopped 29 of 33 and didn't. Outshot 33-19 and still tied in the third, the Sabres found the most Buffalo way to get nothing. Five straight losses, and it's mid-November with fans already checking the lottery odds, the one annual tradition this franchise never misses.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

OTT2WPG1Final: OTT 2, WPG 1

Tyler Boucher, the 10th overall pick in 2021, waited five years for his first NHL game and then scored the winner in it, which is one way to make up for lost time. Ottawa got both of its goals 58 seconds apart early in the second: Drake Batherson's 11th on the power play, then Boucher off a pass from Thomas Chabot. Winnipeg's Viggo Björck answered with his own first NHL goal five minutes later, and that was the end of the scoring, with more than half the game still to play. Linus Ullmark stopped 20 of 21. Stuart Skinner stopped 25 of 27 and got a loss for his trouble. The Senators have won three straight, and the Jets' six-game winning streak is over. Winnipeg had a heater on the line at home and put 21 shots on net, the offensive urgency of a team returning a library book.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

WSH2TBL5Final: WSH 2, TBL 5

Tampa Bay got Brayden Point, Anthony Cirelli and Erik Cernak back in the lineup and had a 3-0 lead before the Capitals finished stretching. Sam O'Reilly scored his first NHL goal 2:11 in, with Point picking up an assist, Charle-Edouard D'Astous made it two, and Jake Guentzel made it three at 13:11. Alex Tuch got one back, Guentzel scored again in the second for his 13th, Ryan Leonard made it 4-2 in the third, and Cirelli closed it into the empty net. John Carlson had three assists against his old team, because of course he did, and Nikita Kucherov had two in his 900th game. Andrei Vasilevskiy stopped 25 of 27; Logan Thompson stopped 20 of 24. Washington has lost three straight for the first time this season, and Alex Ovechkin's goal drought is at 14 games, tying the longest of his career. The man caught Gretzky. Right now he can't catch a break, a bounce or a Tuesday in Tampa.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

TOR3CHI6Final: TOR 3, CHI 6

Make it seven straight losses for the Maple Leafs, and this one came with a former Leaf doing the honors. Easton Cowan put Toronto up 3:22 in, and then the second period got silly: Frank Nazar scored twice, Teddy Blueger tied it 22 seconds after Nazar's second, and Connor Bedard put Chicago ahead for good 35 seconds after that. Tyler Bertuzzi made it 4-2 on a third-period power play, John Tavares cut it to one, and the Blackhawks answered in 12 seconds through Oliver Moore, then again 49 seconds later on Bertuzzi's second of the night. Sam Rinzel had three assists. Spencer Knight stopped 31 of 34; Sergei Bobrovsky stopped 19 of 25, a .760 that explains plenty. Toronto outshot Chicago 34-25 and lost by three. The Leafs have found the one thing harder to watch than their Aprils: their Novembers.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

ANA6STL8Final: ANA 6, STL 8

Fourteen goals, eight different Blues scorers, one Cutter Gauthier hat trick, and a final two minutes that should come with a seat belt. Gauthier scored his 19th, 20th and 21st to run his goal streak to 10 games, one short of Teemu Selanne's Ducks record, added an assist, and lost in regulation. St. Louis broke it open with three goals in 2:58 of the third, from Jake Neighbours, Philip Broberg and Logan Mailloux, whose first of the season capped a career-high three-point night. That made it 7-3 and ended Ville Husso's evening at seven goals on 24 shots. Anaheim then scored three straight, two with the net empty, to get within 7-6 with 41 seconds left, and Pavel Buchnevich hit the empty net three seconds later. Jordan Binnington allowed six on 31 in his first start since Nov. 5 and won comfortably, sort of. The Ducks scored six and never led. Defense in this one was a rumor nobody could confirm.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

NSH3MIN7Final: NSH 3, MIN 7

The Wild's point streak is at 12 games, and the Predators were kind enough to settle this one before the first intermission. Brock Faber scored his first of the season 4:20 in, Blake Coleman and Maxim Shabanov followed, and Matt Boldy made it 4-0 with 81 seconds left in the period, then 5-0 on the power play 59 seconds into the second. Nicolas Hague got Nashville on the board, Marcus Foligno answered 17 seconds later off a pass from brother Nick, and that was it for Justus Annunen: six goals on 20 shots. Juuse Saros stopped 17 of 18 in relief, a nice effort for a game already in the trash. Joel Eriksson Ek had a goal and three assists, Kirill Kaprizov had three assists, and Jesper Wallstedt stopped 25 of 28. Jonathan Marchessault scored in his return for Nashville, whose road trip ended like a bad night on Broadway: early, loud and with somebody getting pulled out of there.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

DAL4VGK3OTFinal: DAL 4, VGK 3 OT

Vegas led 3-1 with 78 seconds left and lost, a collapse so fast the building didn't have time to boo it properly. William Karlsson scored twice and Brett Howden added a third, and the Golden Knights were a minute and change from ending their skid. Then Dallas pulled Jake Oettinger: Wyatt Johnston scored at 18:42, Mikko Rantanen tied it with five seconds on the clock, and Miro Heiskanen, in his first game back after missing five, won it 3:36 into overtime. Rantanen had a goal and three assists, a point on every Stars goal, including Nils Lundkvist's first of the season. Oettinger stopped 24 of 27; Adin Hill stopped 18 of 22. That's three straight losses for Vegas, and the same two teams go again Thursday in the same building. The Knights had this one counted, cashed and halfway to the cage, then learned what every tourist on the Strip already knows: you're not up until you walk out the door.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

CGY5SJS2Final: CGY 5, SJS 2

Jonathan Castagna showed up in San Jose without an NHL goal and left with two, and Simon Nemec scored his first as a Flame, so Calgary's equipment staff spent the night taping pucks. Adam Gaudette put the Sharks up 3:53 in, Matt Coronato tied it 76 seconds later, and Martin Pospisil gave Calgary the lead with 38 seconds left in the first. Nemec's power-play goal early in the second made it 3-1, and Castagna's first made it 4-1 in the third, with an assist to Maxim Tsyplakov in his first game after seven straight in the press box. Mason Marchment scored with the San Jose net empty and a power play going, and Castagna answered into the same empty net. Dustin Wolf stopped 21 of 23; Yaroslav Askarov stopped 24 of 28. The Sharks' future remains bright, mostly because it keeps getting pushed further away.

Alex Newhook and Nick Suzuki, on the power play, also scored, and Lane Hutson assisted on all three. Connor Hellebuyck, who made 25 saves, had been 7-0-0 since his trade from Winnipeg.

nhl.com ↗
BOS
News

Bruins end a three-game skid with a 4-1 win in Detroit; Pastrnak, Zacha and Mittelstadt each have a goal and an assist

Pavel Zacha scored the go-ahead goal on a second-period power play, David Pastrnak added his 10th of the season in the third, and Casey Mittelstadt hit the empty net. Jeremy Swayman made 20 saves on the second night of a back-to-back as Boston moved to 14-7-1. Detroit, 8-11-3, has lost six of its last seven.

nhl.com ↗
NHL
News

NHL unveils the Winter Classic jerseys: Mountain Blue for Utah, white with a burgundy helmet for Colorado

The league and Fanatics revealed both uniforms Wednesday before the Mammoth hosted the Avalanche. Utah wears Mountain Blue with brown and beige and a throwback logo; Colorado wears white and blue with a vintage burgundy C and its first burgundy helmet. The game is Dec. 31 at Rice-Eccles Stadium in Salt Lake City.

nhl.com ↗
PHI
News

Briere calls Friedman's report that the Flyers broke a promise to Cutter Gauthier 'nonsense'

Elliotte Friedman reported that the Flyers broke a promise to Gauthier before his trade request. Danny Briere said on the radio that he was never aware of any promise to Gauthier's camp and that the team wasn't told of any issue. Gauthier, traded to Anaheim in 2024, is tied for the NHL lead with 21 goals.

inquirer.com ↗
PIT
News

Penguins veterans downplay their meeting with Dubas; Letang says the vision has been the same for two years

Sidney Crosby called the meeting quick and short, and Rickard Rakell described it as a check-in on things like team food and travel. Kris Letang said players can only force management's hand by playing well enough to make a push, and Erik Karlsson said the group will make the most of its time together.

Boston College will retire Johnny Gaudreau's No. 13 on Feb. 12

Boston College Hockey announced it will retire the late Johnny Gaudreau's No. 13 on Feb. 12, 2027, The Hockey News reports. Gaudreau had 78 goals and 175 points in three seasons at BC, where he won the Hobey Baker Award and a national title.

Bruins shut out 3-0 by the Kings for a third straight loss; Sturm reunites Pastrnak, Lindholm and Geekie

Marco Sturm shuffled his lines in the third period Tuesday, putting Morgan Geekie and Elias Lindholm back with David Pastrnak, JJ Peterka with Casey Mittelstadt and Pavel Zacha, and Mikey Eyssimont with Fraser Minten and Marat Khusnutdinov. Sturm said the mental part of his team's game isn't its strongest right now. The Bruins play in Detroit tonight, the second night of a back-to-back.

EDM
Lineup

Babcock splits McDavid and Draisaitl for the first time this season with Nugent-Hopkins out again

With Ryan Nugent-Hopkins missing a second straight game, Mike Babcock moved Leon Draisaitl off Connor McDavid's wing during the 5-2 win in Florida to center the second line with Vasily Podkolzin and Kasperi Kapanen. The two had played together through the first 21 games. Babcock said the Oilers didn't have the depth to keep them together and that he liked the new look.

NHL.com's projected lineup has Brett Berard, called up from Laval on Monday, playing his first game for Montreal on a line with Jake Evans and Owen Beck, with Florian Xhekaj a healthy scratch. Alexandre Texier (illness) is questionable. The Canadiens did not hold a morning skate.

Update: Siegenthaler plays through his illness against Montreal; Bratt ties Niedermayer for second in Devils assists

Jonas Siegenthaler, sent home sick from the morning skate, dressed and played 20:06 in the 3-2 loss that ended the Devils' seven-game home winning streak, and Brett Pesce played 22:37 in his return from illness. Jesper Bratt's 364th assist as a Devil tied Scott Niedermayer for second in team history and ran his point streak to nine games.

Lineup

Ruff says the Sabres will dress seven defensemen in Washington; McLeod likely sits and Luukkonen could start

After Wednesday's practice Lindy Ruff said Buffalo will use seven defensemen Thursday and that Ryan McLeod's game 'has to be better'; McLeod, with four points in 19 games, is likely a healthy scratch. Krebs moves up with Ostlund and Quinn, Carrick returns to the fourth line, and Luukkonen, who hasn't played since being pulled Nov. 11, could start after Lyon's three straight.

Manny Malhotra said DeBrusk was given Wednesday off for maintenance, two days after he had a goal and an assist in Utah. Arshdeep Bains took his spot beside Elias Pettersson and Jonathan Lekkerimäki. Meriläinen and Lankinen were both on the ice, and no starter was named for Thursday against the Kraken.

Update: Nazar takes Bedard's spot on the top power play; Blashill wants Bedard to change how he takes faceoffs

At Wednesday's practice Frank Nazar moved to Connor Bedard's left-circle spot on the first power-play unit, with Tyler Bertuzzi sliding into Nazar's place. Coach Jeff Blashill said the team knew there was a high risk of the right shoulder coming back out, and that he wants to keep Bedard at center but have him take faceoffs without lifting his stick.

Ducks put defenseman Travis Mitchell on waivers with Ian Moore back from injury

Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman reports Anaheim placed the 26-year-old on waivers Wednesday. Mitchell has one assist in 14 games and would likely go to AHL San Diego if he clears, now that Ian Moore's return means the Ducks no longer need him on the NHL roster.

BOS 4–1 DET

Boston BruinsBOS14-7-1 · 29 pts31 shots
4
FinalLittle Caesars Arena
1
Detroit Red WingsDET8-11-3 · 19 pts21 shots
1st2nd3rdTBOS0224DET1001

Puckline's Report

Detroit threw itself a 100th birthday party and Boston ate the cake. The Red Wings' Centennial Celebration Game started on script, Lucas Raymond scoring his ninth late in the first, and then the Bruins scored the next four like guests who found the open bar. JJ Peterka tied it early in the second, Pavel Zacha put Boston ahead on the power play, David Pastrnak buried his 10th in the third and Casey Mittelstadt hit the empty net, with Zacha, Pastrnak and Mittelstadt each adding an assist. Mason Lohrei and Morgan Geekie had two helpers apiece. Jeremy Swayman, on the second night of a back-to-back, stopped 20 of 21, which is less a workload than a light jog. Daniil Tarasov made 27 saves on 30 shots and deserved a better party. Boston's three-game skid is over, 4-1. Detroit has a century of history and one goal to show for the night: the franchise turned 100, and the offense skated like it.

By Puckline Prince

Puckline's Report

Lane Hutson didn't score and still ran the building. The Canadiens defenseman set up all three Montreal goals in a 3-2 win in Newark, handing Connor Hellebuyck his first loss as a Devil. The first period was a track meet: Luke Evangelista opened the scoring, Alex Newhook answered 40 seconds later, Timo Meier put New Jersey back in front, and Nick Suzuki tied it on the power play with 42 seconds left before the break. Then everybody remembered defense existed, until Jake Evans scored the winner 6:17 into the third. Jacob Fowler stopped 28 of 30 for Montreal; Hellebuyck stopped 25 of 28. Jack Hughes fired four shots, won a quarter of his faceoffs and went home with nothing. The Devils finally have their goalie in the crease, and the skaters picked that night to take one off. That's New Jersey for you: fix the roof, leave the windows open.

By Puckline Prince

Puckline's Report

Utah's six-game winless streak died the way hockey intended: a fourth-liner's goal and a fistfight four seconds later. Liam O'Brien scored his first of the season 5:22 into the second, Jack McBain and Gabriel Landeskog dropped the gloves before the goal was announced, and the Mammoth rolled to a 4-1 win. Vincent Trocheck added a power-play goal late in the period, O'Brien celebrated by fighting Alex Gagne 38 seconds after that, and Trocheck set up Dmitri Simashev shorthanded a minute into the third. Sebastian Cossa stopped 30 of 31, losing the shutout to Jaden Schwartz with five minutes left, and Kevin Stenlund hit the empty net. Mackenzie Blackwood made 25 saves on 28 shots. Colorado gave up goals at even strength, on the penalty kill and on its own power play. That's not a loss, that's a sampler platter.

LAK @ TOR · 7:00 PM ET

Los Angeles KingsLAK6-11-2 · 14 PTSML -110
@7:00 PM ETThu Nov 19 · Scotiabank Arena
LAK -110MLTOR -110
Toronto Maple LeafsTOR8-13-2 · 18 PTSML -110

Puckline Preview

Seven straight regulation losses, 1-9-0 in the last 10, last in the Atlantic, and now the Maple Leafs come home to the building that watched six of those losses in person. The good news for Toronto: the Kings are here, and Los Angeles is 6-11-2. The bad news: so was everybody else on that homestand. Jim Hiller, who coached the Kings before he coached this, said after Tuesday's 6-3 loss in Chicago that it might be time for lineup changes, which is the hockey version of checking whether the stove is on while the kitchen burns.

The crease is the story. Sergei Bobrovsky has lost six straight starts, and Elliotte Friedman says the Leafs may need to sit him for a couple of weeks; Anthony Stolarz is expected to start after Thursday's morning skate. William Nylander has no points in five games and says he doesn't want to change anything, so Hiller changed it for him: Nylander skated on the third line, with Gavin McKenna moved up beside John Tavares. Darcy Kuemper comes in off his 40th career shutout, 3-0 in Boston, which ended a four-game Kings skid. Artemi Panarin, the Kings' leading scorer, has missed two games while away from the team, with no word on tonight. The last time these two met, in April, Los Angeles won 7-6 in overtime. Nobody in Toronto would turn down six goals right now.

By Puckline Prince

PHI @ OTT · 7:00 PM ET

Philadelphia FlyersPHI7-11-6 · 20 PTSML +155
@7:00 PM ETThu Nov 19 · Canadian Tire Centre
PHI +155MLOTT -184
Ottawa SenatorsOTT14-6-2 · 30 PTSML -184

Puckline Preview

Linus Ullmark is 10-1-0 with a .940 save percentage, and here's the part Ottawa would rather skip: the 1 is Philadelphia. The Flyers, who started the season 0-6-3, got their first win on Oct. 17 by beating Ullmark 3-1, which is like the guy who can't parallel park winning a demolition derby. The Senators took the first meeting 2-1 in their home opener, so the season series is even.

Ottawa (14-6-2) has won three straight, the latest on a storybook goal: Tyler Boucher scored the winner on his first NHL shot Tuesday in Winnipeg. His father, Brian, played his last NHL game as a Flyer, so the family has a rooting interest on both benches. Thomas Chabot blocked a shot late in that game and didn't take another shift, but he was back in his usual spot at Thursday's morning skate.

The Flyers are 7-11-6 and score 2.38 goals a game, but they're 3-1-1 in their last five and Matvei Michkov has points in five straight. Rookie defenseman Oliver Bonk plays his first NHL game in his hometown. The rest of Philadelphia's week has been noise: Travis Konecny trade talk the general manager keeps swatting away, and 'Fire Tocchet' chants at home. Ullmark was in the starter's net at the morning skate; the Flyers haven't named a goalie.

STL @ PIT · 7:00 PM ET

St Louis BluesSTL10-9-2 · 22 PTSML -110
@7:00 PM ETThu Nov 19 · PPG Paints Arena
STL -110MLPIT -110
Pittsburgh PenguinsPIT7-11-2 · 16 PTSML -110

Puckline Preview

The Blues scored eight on Tuesday and needed most of them, outlasting Anaheim 8-6 in a game where defense was a rumor. Now they visit a Penguins team whose general manager spent Wednesday explaining that if things don't steady, he'll start trading veterans for futures. Nothing fires up a room like the boss pricing the furniture.

Pittsburgh is 7-11-2 and hasn't played since Saturday's 4-1 home loss to Ottawa. The players held a meeting, Sidney Crosby still has no extension and says the losing makes the end feel 'more realistic', and Kyle Dubas says the playoffs aren't how this season will be measured, which is convenient. Help may be coming on the back end: Trevor van Riemsdyk practiced next to Kris Letang and could play his first game since Oct. 9, and Ville Koivunen was back on the third line at practice.

St. Louis (10-9-2) kept the same lines after the eight-goal night. Robert Thomas has points in seven straight against the Penguins, and Jimmy Snuggerud, who has 10 goals this season, had four points the last time these teams met, a 7-5 Blues win in April that Pittsburgh led 3-0. Joel Hofer (.922) is the projected starter after Jordan Binnington got the track meet; Arturs Silovs is expected for the Penguins, though neither team has announced a starter.

BUF @ WSH · 7:00 PM ET

Buffalo SabresBUF8-9-4 · 20 PTSML +116
@7:00 PM ETThu Nov 19 · Capital One Arena
BUF +116MLWSH -140
Washington CapitalsWSH10-9-0 · 20 PTSML -140

Puckline Preview

Somebody has to win this one, which will come as news to both teams. Buffalo is winless in five, allowed 21 goals doing it and is 1-5-1 in November. Washington has lost three straight for the first time this season and gave up 17 goals in the three, a stretch Spencer Carbery summed up as 'bonehead mistakes'. It's a get-right game for two teams that have been getting it wrong with real commitment.

The subplot writes itself: Alex Tuch. The former Sabre has 12 goals in 19 games for the Capitals, and when these teams met on Oct. 24 he scored Washington's first goal and the overtime winner in a 4-3 comeback from 2-0 down. He's been sending Buffalo postcards ever since he left. At the other end of the mood chart, Alex Ovechkin, in his final season, has gone 14 games without a goal, matching the longest drought of his career.

Lindy Ruff plans to dress seven defensemen and sit Ryan McLeod, and Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen could get the net for the first time since he was pulled on Nov. 11; Alex Lyon has lost all three starts since returning. Mattias Samuelsson is questionable after a maintenance day. Logan Thompson is the projected Capitals starter.

MTL @ CAR · 7:00 PM ET

Montreal CanadiensMTL13-5-4 · 30 PTSML +220
@7:00 PM ETThu Nov 19 · Lenovo Center
MTL +220MLCAR -275
Carolina HurricanesCAR16-3-2 · 34 PTSML -275

Puckline Preview

Montreal's reward for winning in New Jersey last night is a flight to Raleigh to play the defending champions on no rest. The Hurricanes are 16-3-2, plus-40, scoring 4.14 goals a game, and they've had since Saturday to recover from sweeping Seattle in Helsinki. The Canadiens have had since about 10 p.m.

These two know each other. Carolina beat Montreal in five games in last spring's Eastern Conference Final on the way to the Stanley Cup, then spoiled the Canadiens' home opener 6-4 on Oct. 6, outshooting them 17-4 in the second period. Zachary Bolduc scored twice that night; he left Wednesday's game after two periods and there's been no update. Chris Kreider, Josh Anderson, Ivan Demidov and Mike Matheson are already out.

What the Canadiens do have is Lane Hutson, who set up all three goals in the 3-2 win over the Devils, and a power play that finally scored after a 1-for-15 stretch, which in Montreal counts as a heater. Jacob Fowler played last night, so Jakub Dobes is the likely starter. Pyotr Kochetkov (12-1-0) sat out practice Tuesday, returned Wednesday and is expected in the Carolina net. Jackson Blake brings an 11-game point streak.

NYI @ WPG · 7:00 PM ET

New York IslandersNYI10-6-4 · 24 PTSML -110
@7:00 PM ETThu Nov 19 · Canada Life Centre
NYI -110MLWPG -110
Winnipeg JetsWPG10-9-3 · 23 PTSML -110

Puckline Preview

The Islanders' leading scorer is a defenseman, and on Tuesday he did something no Islanders defenseman had done since Denis Potvin in 1982: Matthew Schaefer scored a hat trick in a 5-1 win over Columbus. He has 24 points in 20 games, New York has won three straight by a combined 16-5, and Simon Holmstrom had a hat trick of his own on Saturday. Long Island hasn't been this fun since people were still mad about the fisherman jersey.

Winnipeg has been a roller coaster with a seat belt problem: nine straight without a win, then six straight wins, then a 2-1 home loss to Ottawa on Tuesday in which the Jets managed 21 shots. This is the team that traded Connor Hellebuyck to New Jersey in October, and Stuart Skinner, the projected starter, carries an .883 save percentage. Kyle Connor has 17 goals and Mark Scheifele has 26 points, so there's offense at the top; it's the other end that keeps the rides interesting.

It's the first meeting of the season. Logan Stanley, the former Jet now on the Islanders' blue line, is day to day and may miss his return to Winnipeg, and Jean-Gabriel Pageau is questionable. Ilya Sorokin is expected for New York.

EDM @ TBL · 7:30 PM ET

Edmonton OilersEDM17-3-3 · 37 PTSML +118
@7:30 PM ETThu Nov 19 · Benchmark International Arena
EDM +118MLTBL -142
Tampa Bay LightningTBL14-5-2 · 30 PTSML -142

Puckline Preview

The best game on the board. Edmonton has won six straight, is 17-3-3 and hasn't lost in regulation on the road all season (10-0-1). Tampa Bay is 14-5-2, first in the Atlantic and 9-1-0 at home. Something has to give, and it's probably a goalie's evening.

Connor McDavid has a point in all 23 games and 55 on the season, a pace that makes the rest of the league look like it's playing a different sport. Leon Draisaitl has 21 goals. Mike Babcock split the two on Tuesday for the first time this season with Ryan Nugent-Hopkins out sick, and Vasily Podkolzin scored twice beside Draisaitl; Nugent-Hopkins is day to day. The last time these teams met, in March, Nikita Kucherov put up four points in a 5-2 Lightning win in Edmonton and passed McDavid for the scoring lead, so somebody's been keeping the receipt.

Tampa Bay got Brayden Point, Anthony Cirelli and Erik Cernak back on Tuesday but is thin again up front: Brandon Hagel is day to day, Zemgus Girgensons left that game early and Conor Geekie is on injured reserve. Andrei Vasilevskiy is expected in net. Edmonton has alternated Devon Levi (10-1-0) and Tristan Jarry and hasn't named a starter. Meanwhile Jake Walman, in year one of a seven-year contract, has been a healthy scratch since Nov. 5. Expensive seat.

CBJ @ CHI · 8:00 PM ET

Columbus Blue JacketsCBJ7-12-0 · 14 PTSML -166
@8:00 PM ETThu Nov 19 · United Center
CBJ -166MLCHI +138
Chicago BlackhawksCHI6-13-2 · 14 PTSML +138

Puckline Preview

Chicago has lost seven straight to Columbus, outscored 35-12, going back to the last day of 2022. Read that again: the Blue Jackets, who have dropped five in a row in regulation by a combined 21-8 and are 1-6-0 on the road, own somebody. Everyone needs a hobby.

The Blackhawks (6-13-2) are the team with a pulse this week, 2-0-1 in their last three with a 6-3 win over Toronto on the 100th anniversary of the franchise's first game. It came at a cost: Connor Bedard hurt his right shoulder on a faceoff in the third period, there's no timeline, and he isn't expected to play. Anton Frondell moved up to his top-line spot at practice, and Frank Nazar, who has five of his 10 goals in the last three games, took his place on the first power play.

Columbus (7-12-0) gets Rick Bowness back behind the bench after three games away, all losses, and Isac Lundestrom is off long-term injured reserve and available for his season debut. Zach Werenski has a point in all seven road games. The goalies could both use a hug: Jet Greaves has lost six straight starts and Spencer Knight has been leaky over his last six. Both are projected, neither confirmed.

MIN @ CGY · 8:00 PM ET

Minnesota WildMIN16-3-4 · 36 PTSML -230
@8:00 PM ETThu Nov 19 · Scotiabank Saddledome
MIN -230MLCGY +188
Calgary FlamesCGY10-11-1 · 21 PTSML +188

Puckline Preview

Minnesota hasn't lost in regulation in four weeks. The last team to do it? These Flames, 2-1 at the Saddledome on Oct. 22, when Devin Cooley stopped 36 of 37 and Calgary's power play scored twice. Since then the Wild are 10-0-2, and they've scored 18 goals in their last three games. Calgary has won six of the last eight meetings anyway, and John Hynes says his team hasn't played well against the Flames. Every juggernaut has a weird cousin it can't beat at ping-pong.

The numbers say this shouldn't be close to a rivalry. Minnesota is 16-3-4 and plus-32; Kirill Kaprizov has 40 points and a 12-game point streak, Quinn Hughes has a 12-gamer of his own, and Jesper Wallstedt is 15-2-3 with a 1.99 goals-against average. Calgary is 10-11-1, minus-20 and scores 2.55 goals a game, the kind of offense that fits in a carry-on.

But the Flames come home off a 5-2 win in San Jose in which Jonathan Castagna scored his first two NHL goals, and they haven't said whether Cooley or Dustin Wolf starts. Filip Gustavsson is cleared and practicing with the Wild but isn't available tonight, and Jonathan Huberdeau played his first game since February on Wednesday, on a conditioning loan with the AHL Wranglers.

ANA @ COL · 9:00 PM ET

Anaheim DucksANA11-10-1 · 23 PTSML +114
@9:00 PM ETThu Nov 19 · Ball Arena
ANA +114MLCOL -137
Colorado AvalancheCOL12-7-3 · 27 PTSML -137

Puckline Preview

Cutter Gauthier has scored in 10 straight games. One more tonight ties Teemu Selanne's Ducks record of 11, set in 1997, and he's doing it in bulk: a hat trick on Tuesday, 21 goals on the season. The Ducks lost that game 8-6 in St. Louis, because Anaheim treats defense the way most people treat the terms and conditions. Ville Husso gave up seven goals on 24 shots before he was pulled, so Lukas Dostal may get the net; the Ducks haven't said.

Colorado would like a quiet night and isn't getting one. The Avalanche lost 4-1 in Utah on Wednesday, went 0-for-4 on the power play, gave up a shorthanded goal and won 31 percent of the faceoffs, and now play the second half of a back-to-back. Nathan MacKinnon and Cale Makar are both out, and Gavin Brindley left the Utah game in the first period with no update since. Scott Wedgewood is the likely starter after Mackenzie Blackwood played last night.

Even so, this is a 12-7-3 team that won the last meeting 5-1 in Anaheim in March. The Ducks (11-10-1) score 3.86 goals a game and have a goal differential of exactly zero, the most Anaheim stat there is: every goal they've scored, they've personally handed back. Beckett Sennecke, who sat out Tuesday with an illness, is day to day.

Puckline Preview

The Canucks are on a winning streak. It's two games, it's their first of the season, and at 5-17-1 they will take it and frame it. Vancouver won 6-3 in Vegas on Sunday and 3-2 in Utah on Monday, its first win ever against the Mammoth, and Brock Boeser has points in eight straight. Now comes the part of the trip where history gets rude: Seattle has points in nine straight against Vancouver (7-0-2) and has outscored the Canucks 40-22 doing it. For a rivalry that's supposed to be about geography, it's mostly been about one team's lunch money.

The Kraken (9-8-1) aren't exactly rolling, though. They've lost three straight, the last two to Carolina in Helsinki by 4-1 and 5-1, which is a long way to fly to score twice. Joey Daccord has been pulled in three of his last seven starts and Lane Lambert says he has to be better; the team site's own projected lineup has Philipp Grubauer in net tonight. Jared McCann is still out, and Seattle starts a run of six games in nine days.

For Vancouver, Jake DeBrusk missed Wednesday's practice for maintenance, with Arshdeep Bains skating in his spot beside Elias Pettersson. Leevi Meriläinen is the projected starter.

DAL @ VGK · 10:00 PM ET

Dallas StarsDAL13-6-2 · 28 PTSML +102
@10:00 PM ETThu Nov 19 · T-Mobile Arena
DAL +102MLVGK -122
Vegas Golden KnightsVGK13-6-4 · 30 PTSML -122

Puckline Preview

Same teams, same building, two nights later, and Vegas has had 48 hours to think about what it did. On Tuesday the Golden Knights led Dallas 3-1 with under two minutes left and lost 4-3 in overtime: Wyatt Johnston scored with the goalie pulled at 18:42, Mikko Rantanen tied it with about five seconds to go, and Miro Heiskanen, in his first game back after missing five, won it in overtime. It was the first time in franchise history Vegas lost after leading by two with two minutes to play. In a town built on people who don't know when to cash out, that's on brand.

The Golden Knights (13-6-4) have now lost three straight, including a 6-3 home loss to Vancouver, and close their longest homestand of the season tonight still without Noah Hanifin. Mitch Marner is one assist from 600. Adin Hill and Carter Hart have alternated starts and nobody's been named.

Dallas (13-6-2) has won three in a row and five of its last six against Vegas, and each of the last seven meetings was decided by one goal, so pack a lunch. Rantanen had four points on Tuesday, and Jake Oettinger, who leads the league with four shutouts, is the projected starter. The Stars are missing Tyler Myers and Matt Duchene.
